sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In lesson 9 you said what is happening now: I am reading. Now you'll say what was happening at a moment in the past: «I was reading a comic book», «I was cleaning my boots when you called», «she was sniffing the flowers while I was talking».

examples.en: I was reading a comic book.
examples.translation: At that moment, I was in the middle of reading.

examples.en: They were doing a jigsaw puzzle.
examples.translation: At that moment, they were putting the puzzle together.

examples.en: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.
examples.translation: Your call came in the middle of my cleaning.

examples.en: She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.
examples.translation: Both things went on at the same time.

blocks.text: This is lesson 9 moved into the past: use was / were instead of am / is / are, and keep the -ing. I was reading — I was in the middle of reading. They were doing a puzzle.

examples.en: I was reading a comic book.
examples.translation: At that moment, I was in the middle of reading.

examples.en: She was using a colouring book.
examples.translation: She was colouring pictures.

examples.en: I was cooking fried rice.
examples.translation: I was in the middle of cooking rice.

examples.en: We were eating a spring roll.
examples.translation: We were in the middle of eating.

examples.en: They were watching the soap bubbles.
examples.translation: Their eyes were on the bubbles.

fixes.wrong: I was read a comic book.
fixes.right: I was reading a comic book.
I was reading a comic book.

fixes.wrong: They was doing a jigsaw puzzle.
fixes.right: They were doing a jigsaw puzzle.

drill.why: They in the past takes were; the -ing is already there.

blocks.text: Put «not» after the clip, as always: I wasn't playing, they weren't watching. wasn't means was not, weren't means were not. The -ing stays.

examples.en: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.
examples.translation: I was doing something else at that time.

examples.en: I wasn't writing in the homework diary.
examples.translation: My homework diary stayed closed.

examples.en: I wasn't watching the robin.
examples.translation: My eyes weren't on the bird.

fixes.wrong: I didn't playing on the bouncy castle.
fixes.right: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.

fixes.wrong: I wasn't play on the bouncy castle.
fixes.right: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.

blocks.text: Put the clip first, like in lessons 2 and 9: Were you playing in the paddling pool? Was he watching the owl? Don't use did here: Did you playing is wrong.

examples.en: Were you playing in the paddling pool?
examples.translation: You ask what they were doing at that time.

examples.en: Was he jumping on the trampoline?
examples.translation: You ask what he was doing at that time.

examples.en: Were you using the workbook?
examples.translation: You ask if the workbook was open in front of them.

examples.en: Was he watching the owl?
examples.translation: You ask if his eyes were on the owl.

fixes.wrong: Did you playing in the paddling pool?
fixes.right: Were you playing in the paddling pool?

fixes.wrong: You were playing in the paddling pool?
fixes.right: Were you playing in the paddling pool?

drill.question: Ask if he was watching the owl at that time. Which is correct?
drill.explain: With -ing, the question starts with was or were, not did.

blocks.text: Use this form to paint the background: what people were doing when the story started. I was changing a flat tyre. It's not a single event, but something that was going on.

examples.en: I was changing a flat tyre.
examples.translation: I was in the middle of putting on a new tyre.

examples.en: He was checking the windscreen wiper.
examples.translation: He was looking at the wiper on the car window.

examples.en: We were cleaning the rear-view mirror.
examples.translation: We were in the middle of cleaning the mirror.

examples.en: She was packing the nappy bag.
examples.translation: She was putting things into the baby bag.

sections.title: when — something happened in the middle

blocks.text: If something happened in the middle of an action, the long action uses was / were + -ing, and the short event uses the simple past after when: I was cleaning my boots when you called. The call was short and stopped the cleaning.

examples.en: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.
examples.translation: Your call came in the middle of my cleaning.

examples.en: She was packing her ballet flats when I called.
examples.translation: My call came while she was packing.

examples.en: We were looking for an insole when you arrived.
examples.translation: You came in while we were looking.

examples.en: She was drawing a piece of driftwood when I arrived.
examples.translation: I came in while she was drawing.

fixes.wrong: I cleaned my ankle boots when you were calling.
fixes.right: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.

fixes.wrong: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you were call.
fixes.right: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.

drill.prompt: Say that you were looking for an insole when they arrived.

sections.title: while — two actions at the same time

blocks.text: while means «during the time that». Use it when two actions were going on at the same time. Both parts use was / were + -ing: She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.

examples.en: I was looking up while you were taking a photo.
examples.translation: Both things happened at the same time.

examples.en: She was sniffing the flowers while I was talking.
examples.translation: Both things happened at the same time.

examples.en: We were giggling while he was telling the story.
examples.translation: We laughed quietly during his story.

examples.en: I was cutting celery while you were cooking.
examples.translation: We were both busy in the kitchen at once.

blocks.text: A short event that interrupts: when + simple past — when you called. A long action at the same time: while + was / were + -ing — while you were cooking.

examples.en: We were watching a wasp when you called.
examples.translation: Your call came in the middle.

examples.en: I was watching a butterfly while you were taking a photo.
examples.translation: Both things went on together.

examples.en: I was turning around when you called my name.
examples.translation: You said my name as I turned.

drill.why: Two actions were going on at the same time: while.

fixes.wrong: I was read a comic book.
fixes.right: I was reading a comic book.

fixes.wrong: They was doing a jigsaw puzzle.
fixes.right: They were doing a jigsaw puzzle.

fixes.wrong: I didn't playing on the bouncy castle.
fixes.right: I wasn't playing on the bouncy castle.

fixes.wrong: Did you playing in the paddling pool?
fixes.right: Were you playing in the paddling pool?

fixes.wrong: I cleaned my ankle boots when you were calling.
fixes.right: I was cleaning my ankle boots when you called.

blocks.text: An action going on in the past: was / were + -ing. A short event that interrupted it: simple past after when. did doesn't go with -ing.
Going on in the past: was / were + -ing. «Not»: wasn't / weren't. Questions: Was…? Were…? Interrupted: when + simple past. At the same time: while + was / were + -ing.

examples.en: I was filling a spray bottle.
examples.translation: I was putting water into a spray bottle.

examples.en: Were you taking a photo of the woodpecker?
examples.translation: You ask what they were doing at that time.

examples.en: I was looking at a starfish when you called.
examples.translation: Your call came while I was looking.

examples.en: I was using a glue stick while you were drawing.
examples.translation: We were both busy at the same time.
